title: Brother and Navy service
summary: His brother played saxophone; both joined the Navy as musicians and he was discharged for an essential job.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Oh, do you have any other members of the family that played? I forgot to ask.
My brother played saxophone. He still played?
Did he ever play professionally around here much?

No, not too much, no. He didn't bother me as much. See, we both went in the Navy. I didn't have to go, but I took that opportunity and went as a musician, see. I came out, I went in as a musician second class, with a written, and I finished up musician first class. My reason for coming out when they passed that law when you was over forty-something I think it was, they let you go if you had an essential job. Well, at that time I was driving at the Port of Imbalcation. I had an essential job, so they discharged me.
Is your brother older or younger than you?
He's older. Older. He's born 1900. He'll be 60 in October. Can you think of anything, Ralph?
